_about: Shared by the browser sim and the motor bridge. Joint angles are the URDF's (degrees); lengths in mm. Geometry comes from web/meshes/manifest.json (tools/import_urdf.py). Restart the bridge after editing.

mass_kg._note: Used for the gravity readout and the optional gravity feed-forward. The URDF's inertials are placeholders (~0.1 g per part), so these are estimates: elbow_assembly = IM6014 (535 g, published) + its cage; links = two tubes + clamps. Weigh your parts and update before enabling gravity_ff.

_joint_limits_note: J1: 180 deg total (+-90 about the URDF zero) for wire management; no mechanical stop, so this is a soft limit that relies on the J1 calibration. J2 before calibration: the CAD contacts (-88.94 tube clamp on a turret nut, +51.54 elbow cage on the table) minus 4 deg; calibration replaces them with the measured contacts minus calibration.limit_margin_deg. J3: 60..390 (390 = 30 past the CAD pose at 360): its absolute-encoder reading is mapped within +-180 of the middle of these limits, so the 30 deg it cannot reach sits at 'forearm folded back along the upper arm', a pose the arm never needs.

calibration._note: Contact-seek settings used by Calibrate. kp/kd are per joint while seeking (Nm/rad, Nm/(rad/s)).

bus._note: All three IDs on one RS-485 channel by default. A joint may set its own "port" to use another FT4232H channel.
